A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CALM-PDE by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE prediction experiments, computational measurements, component ablations and qualitative analyses in Section 6 and Appendices K–M.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds sensitivity studies, stationary-PDE experiments, reconstruction results and mesh-scaling measurements. Some comparator scores in Appendix O are explicitly borrowed from prior work.

M1.justification: The CALM layers, adaptive query points, kernel modulation, latent Transformer and main training procedure remain unchanged. Appendix O.2 evaluates the existing encoder-decoder separately; self-reconstruction training was already discussed in v1 Section 4.3.

E1.justification: The original time-dependent fluid benchmarks are retained. Appendix O.1 adds stationary airfoil and elasticity geometry-to-field tasks, substantially extending task and domain coverage. The new airfoil task varies geometry, unlike the retained time-dependent airfoil benchmark with fixed geometry.

E2.justification: F-FNO and AROMA join the regular- and irregular-mesh accuracy comparisons in Tables 1–2 and 21–22. Table 23 additionally includes Galerkin Transformer, GNOT, ONO and Transolver in comparisons using literature scores. Figure 4 and Table 3 retain their original efficiency comparators.

E3.justification: v2 adds temperature and query-count sweeps, stationary-task protocols, reconstruction evaluation and single-step output-grid scaling from 64×64 to 512×512 at batch size 32. Newly evaluated AROMA configurations use shortened training budgets. Appendix H.1 also changes the last 200 Navier–Stokes samples from 'training' to 'testing'; this corrects the reported split without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and visual diagnostics, Appendix K tests temperature sensitivity, M.5 examines latent capacity versus error and training time, O.2 isolates reconstruction quality, and O.3 measures computational scaling with output mesh size. These address several previously untested questions.

E5.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation standard deviations are retained, and the added baseline rows follow that convention. However, the new temperature and latent-size studies report only point estimates, unlike v1's ablation tables, making uncertainty reporting less consistent. No explicit run counts, seed identifiers or statistical tests are added.

E6.justification: Retained numerical results are unchanged, but added comparators alter rankings: CALM-PDE's cylinder error remains 0.1186 while newly included AROMA achieves 0.1139; on 3D Navier–Stokes, F-FNO's 0.6466 places CALM-PDE's unchanged 0.6761 third instead of second. Tables 14, 20 and 23–26 add sensitivity, stationary-task, reconstruction and scaling results, rather than improvements to matched existing scores.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a computational-complexity argument comparing O(p N N' d) CALM-layer computations with O(N N' d) unrestricted attention computations. Existing mathematical definitions, model equations and NODE derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction localizes novelty more explicitly to the encoder and decoder instead of describing the whole architecture as novel. The conclusion adds an explicit qualification that CALM-PDE does not consistently surpass all baselines. The abstract's central contribution and efficiency claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning hyperparameter robustness and possible overfitting or diminishing returns at larger latent sizes. Appendix O.3 explicitly limits its large-mesh evidence to computational costs. Section K's new claim of identical receptive-field percentiles across 2D experiments overstates Table 13, which retains differing values. Section 7's principal limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Tables 8, 12 and 24 add detailed configurations for F-FNO, AROMA and the stationary CALM-PDE experiments, including training budgets, dimensions and learning rates. v2 also documents a latent-size selection rationale and settings for the new scaling study. Existing core implementation details and the code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Factorized Fourier Neural Operators, Transolver and orthogonal-attention operator learning, with accompanying comparator discussion. Novelty is more specifically attributed to the encoder-decoder. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for already cited works, while the main related-work analysis remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. Changes comprise localized introduction and conclusion edits, additional explanatory and experimental subsections, updated appendix navigation and publication-header text. There is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially: eight new tables document configurations, sensitivity studies and Appendix O experiments, while four accuracy tables gain baseline rows. Existing figures are retained, with some redistributed across pages; these relocations do not constitute new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Including F-FNO and AROMA makes the competitive assessment more complete, and the revised conclusion acknowledges the resulting limitations. New diagnostic studies and configuration details improve empirical support and transparency. These gains are tempered by shortened AROMA training, literature-sourced appendix comparisons, missing uncertainty in new studies and Section K's overstatement of hyperparameter uniformity.
